title: How Medical VLMs Underutilize Their Vision Encoders: A Dermatology Perspective
abstract: arXiv:2609.36557v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Medical Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show significant promise for clinical image understanding, offering accurate diagnosis with interpretable reasoning. However, a critical performance gap exists between their strong vision encoders and the full multimodal model: in dermatology, the MedSigLIP encoder outperforms MedGemma by an average of 10.26 percentage points even when both use zero target-task labels; few-shot linear probing provides further evidence of strong visual representations. This gap motivates an investigation of how visual information is used in end-to-end diagnosis and why plausible-sounding predictions can lack grounding in image evidence. Using dermatology as our primary testbed, we systematically investigate three hypotheses for this phenomenon. We further provide a mechanistic analysis of the model's internal attention patterns, showing that a simple describe-then-decide prompting strategy increases vision attention

translated_title: 医学视觉语言模型如何未充分利用其视觉编码器：来自皮肤病学的视角
translated_abstract: 医学视觉语言模型在临床图像理解方面展现出巨大潜力，能够通过可解释的推理提供准确的诊断。然而，在其强大的视觉编码器与完整的多模态模型之间存在关键的性能差距：在皮肤病学领域，即使两者都使用零目标任务标签，MedSigLIP编码器的性能平均仍超出MedGemma 10.26个百分点；少样本线性探测进一步证实了其强大的视觉表征能力。这一差距促使我们研究视觉信息在端到端诊断中是如何被利用的，以及为什么听起来合理的预测可能缺乏图像证据的支持。以皮肤病学作为主要测试平台，我们系统地研究了这一现象的三个假设。我们进一步对模型的内部注意力模式进行了机制分析，结果表明一种简单的“先描述后决策”提示策略可以增加模型对视觉信息的注意力。
tldr: 该研究揭示了医学视觉语言模型中强大的视觉编码器与完整多模态模型之间存在显著的性能差距，并通过机制分析表明，简单的“先描述后决策”提示策略可以增加模型对视觉证据的注意力利用。
en_tdlr: This study reveals a significant performance gap between strong vision encoders and full multimodal medical VLMs, and through mechanistic analysis demonstrates that a simple describe-then-decide prompting strategy increases the model's utilization of visual attention.
